$comment: Conformance suite of the XY Forever serial protocol v1 (spec: protocol/v1.json, protocol/v1.json). The behaviour a v1 device must show, as data: each case is a named exchange that every client runs the same way (Python: scripts/conformance.py; TypeScript: clients/ts/test/conformance.ts) against the simulator or a device. scripts/protogen.py validates this file against the spec (xy_forever/conformance.py) and the coverage rules; `syntax` documents every keyword. Frame-level vectors stay in v1.json (`streams`) and are referenced by name, not copied.
doc: `protocol/v1.conformance.json` holds the conformance suite: the behaviour a v1 device must show, as data that any client can run. Each case is a named exchange: preconditions (`given`: a fresh boot before `hello`, files in the test area, simulator faults), requests by command name and field values (or raw bytes for malformed input and frame-level tests), and what must come back (status, field values, limits such as the device's `read=`), including reads that show what did not change. Every case says what it does (`effects`: none means read-only; `staging`, `writes_test_area`, `restarts`, `writes_device`, `boots_os`), what it needs (`needs`: simulator control, fixtures) and whether it is safe on a real device (`real_device`, else `why_not`). The keywords are documented in the file's `syntax` object.

A third-party client conforms when it runs every case with its own codec and transport: send the requests in order, one at a time, and check each expectation. Two runners exist: `python3 scripts/conformance.py --sim 127.0.0.1:7341` (or without `--sim` for the OP-XY, where only cases marked safe run and a guard refuses any request that could change more than the test area `/yaffs2/xy-forever/log/conformance/`), and `node clients/ts/test/conformance.ts --sim 127.0.0.1:7341` for the TypeScript module. Both read the same file; `--check` only interprets every case.

syntax.case: name, doc, rules (spec rule names it shows), variant (`v1`, default, or `pre_v1`: the device its HELLO must announce), effects, needs, real_device, why_not (when real_device is false), given, steps
syntax.effects: staging: uses processor B's RAM staging; writes_test_area: writes files under test_area; restarts: the device restarts; writes_device: changes stored state outside test_area (boot partition, default); boots_os: leaves the menu for the default firmware. None: read-only
syntax.needs: sim_control: the simulator's control port (HOST:PORT+1); sim_library: the simulator's seeded library (opxy-121 default, opxy-121-stock); fixture:NAME: a local file the runner is given (--fixture NAME=PATH)
syntax.given: boot: `fresh` = restart the device first (hello, device.reboot target 2) so the case starts before any hello; hello: false = do not send hello after connecting (only with a fresh boot); files: [{path, data}] written to the test area first (stage, then file.write_staged); faults: {name: value} set on the simulator's control port, reset after the case
syntax.steps: one action each: send (a command name, with fields or a raw payload), send_type (a request type no command uses, with an optional payload), send_bytes (raw bytes for the frame layer), stream (a to_device stream of v1.json, by name), each_type (`unlisted`: every request type below 0x80 that neither cmds nor the spec lists), stage (bytes: stage.begin, stage.data in put_chunk pieces, stage.end, each ok), write ({path, data}: stage, then file.write_staged, ok with written and readback_crc), disconnect (the connection must drop within timing.gone_ms), reconnect ({hello}: the port must come back within timing.back_ms; hello defaults to true; optional ready: true waits for storage.space v1 ok when HELLO advertises that command: retry only busy within the runner reply cap, fail other statuses, then return to the case), sim (a line for the simulator's control port), plus optional repeat ({var, from, to, step}: the step for var = from, from + step, ... below to), seq (for send) and doc
syntax.expect: status (a name, or a list of acceptable names), alone (true: nothing after the status), fields ({name: value or constraint}, decoded with the command's reply layout, leniently), hello ({prefix, keys: {name: value or constraint}, lacks: [keys], answers: [commands whose type cmds must list], pre_v1}), save ({var: field}), events ({log: {min}}: log events received while waiting), replies (after send_bytes: the replies, [{type, seq, status}], in order, and nothing else before a hello the runner sends after them), none_within_ms (after send_bytes: no frame arrives in this time)
syntax.values: a number; a string (text for cstr/text fields, lowercase hex for bytes, rest and raw payloads); {text}: a string (UTF-8 where bytes are wanted); {hex}; {fill, count}: count bytes of value fill; {ramp: n}: n bytes 0, 1, ... 255, 0, ...; {prefix, fill, length}: prefix padded with fill to length bytes; {blob, from, length}: a named blob or a slice (clamped at its end); {size|crc32|sha256: blob}; {const: name}: a constant of v1.json; {hello: key}: a key of the last hello reply; {var: name}; {frame: {type, seq, payload}, from, length}: an encoded frame or a slice; {concat: [values]}: bytes. const, hello, var and size take `plus`
syntax.constraints: an object with any of len, len_min, len_max (bytes or characters of the value), min, max (numbers), matches (a regular expression, as JavaScript and Python read it), one_of (values); any other value means equal
syntax.blobs: named data for values: text, hex, fill/count, ramp, or fixture (a local file the runner is given; cases using it need fixture:NAME)
syntax.uncovered: statuses a command documents, and spec rules, that no case shows, each with why

cases.name: dev.a_rehearsal/readonly-status-and-version
cases.why_not: Developer A staging is qualified offline before hardware use.
cases.doc: Status is read-only; malformed and future versions refuse before starting a transfer.

cases.name: hello/before-hello
cases.doc: Until it has answered a hello since it started, the device answers every other request with state and does nothing: the stage.begin sent before hello announced nothing.

cases.name: hello/reply
cases.doc: The v1 hello text: XYF1, then key=value items; the limits are the spec's constants and cmds lists every command each build answers.

cases.name: hello/repeat
cases.doc: A build's hello text never changes while it runs, and the device ignores a hello payload.

cases.name: hello/unlisted-types
cases.doc: Every request type that cmds does not list (and no command of the spec uses) gets unsupported, the status alone.

cases.name: hello/pre-v1
cases.doc: A pre-v1 device sends proto=1 and no cmds; a client treats every 1.0 command as answered.

cases.name: diag.status/blocks
cases.doc: The developer status reply: blocks of {u32 magic, u32 bytes, bytes}; the request payload is ignored.

cases.name: file.read/ranged-and-whole
cases.doc: A ranged read returns at most the device's read= bytes; the whole form of a small file returns the same bytes.

cases.name: file.read/ranges-to-the-end
cases.doc: Ranges of max_read bytes read a file; the last range is short, and an offset at or past the end is ok with no data.

cases.name: file.read/not-found
cases.doc: A file that does not exist: not_found, the status alone.

cases.name: file.read/bad-paths
cases.doc: A path outside /yaffs2/, with an empty, . or .. part, or without its NUL is bad_request.

cases.name: file.read/refused-control-bytes
cases.doc: A well-formed path with a control byte (below 0x20, or 0x7F) is refused by the device's file policy before anything is sent to storage.

cases.name: file.read/limits
cases.doc: length is 1 to max_read; the path is at most max_path bytes with its NUL; offset without length is bad_request (optional fields are all or none).

cases.name: file.read/whole-too-large
cases.doc: The whole form of a file above max_data: too_large, the status alone (nothing large is sent).

cases.name: file.read/whole-above-read
cases.why_not: a reply above the device's read= limit (2.5 KiB) hung the device
cases.doc: The whole form returns a file of up to max_data bytes in one reply.

cases.name: screen.read/screenshot
cases.doc: A screenshot: offsets 0, 1024, ... until 245760 bytes, each reply max_read pixel bytes and the same framebuffer address.

cases.name: screen.read/edges
cases.doc: The last byte reads 1 byte; an offset past the end or a request that is not 4 bytes is range, with the framebuffer address.

cases.name: stage/complete-then-replaced
cases.doc: stage.begin, stage.data in order, stage.end: ok. A new stage.begin forgets the complete staging: once the new one is discarded, nothing is staged.

cases.name: stage/begin-limits
cases.doc: stage.begin: a wrong length is bad_request; a size of 0 or above max_stage is too_large; max_stage itself is accepted.

cases.name: stage/data-errors
cases.doc: stage.data: state without an announced staging or without data; range out of order or past the announced size.

cases.name: stage/end-errors
cases.doc: stage.end checks the announced CRC-32 (crc) and SHA-256 (sha); after any error the staging is discarded.

cases.name: stage/failed-begin
cases.doc: A stage.begin that fails forgets the earlier staging too: stage.data and stage.end are then state.

cases.name: stage/end-repeated
cases.doc: A second stage.end after an ok one (a retry after a lost reply) is ok again and keeps the staging: file.write_staged still writes it.

cases.name: stage/data-resend
cases.doc: stage.data resending bytes already received, unchanged (a retry after a lost reply), is ok with received unchanged; changed bytes at an old offset are range.

cases.name: stage/max-payload
cases.why_not: a frame above about 2 KiB overflowed the device's USB receive buffer (tools send put_chunk bytes)
cases.doc: A request of max_payload bytes (stage.data with 4156 data bytes) is one frame the device accepts.

cases.name: stage/lost-on-restart
cases.doc: Staging lives in RAM: after device.reboot nothing is staged, and nothing can be written from it.

cases.name: file.write_staged/write-and-read-back
cases.doc: A staged image written to the test area: ok with the bytes written and the CRC-32 read back; ranged reads return it.

cases.name: file.write_staged/refused
cases.doc: 1.13: the marker or a path in /yaffs2/upgrade (any case), a folder path (trailing /), a .. part or a control byte is refused (written 0), checked before the staging and the token; the file stays absent.

cases.name: file.write_staged/content
cases.why_not: writes the OS's content folder, outside the test area (the device pass writes one scratch file there)
cases.doc: 1.7: the content folder is in the write area: a file written, read back, replaced and deleted; a folder made and removed.

cases.name: file.write_staged/bad-request
cases.doc: A request whose length does not match its path (one byte short, or empty) is bad_request, with written 0.

cases.name: file.write_staged/state
cases.doc: Without a complete staging: state, sent with the command's fields (written 0), not alone; nothing is written.

cases.name: file.write_staged/sha
cases.doc: A confirmation token that is not the staged image's SHA-256: sha, written 0; the file stays absent.

cases.name: file.write_staged/onto-a-folder
cases.doc: Writing to a path that is a folder: storage, written 0.

cases.name: file.write_staged/storage-full
cases.why_not: needs the simulator's storage fault (space)
cases.doc: Storage that fills up during the write: storage.

cases.name: file.write_staged/utf8-name
cases.doc: File names are UTF-8: written and read back byte for byte.

cases.name: file.list/folder-and-pages
cases.doc: A folder with a file and a folder: two entries (kind, size, name), no more; skip passes over entries, and past the end a page is empty.

cases.name: file.list/utf8-name
cases.doc: Names come back as their UTF-8 bytes with an explicit length: café.txt is 9 bytes.

cases.name: file.list/errors
cases.doc: A path the file policy refuses is refused; a missing folder is not_found; a request whose length does not match its path is bad_request.

cases.name: file.delete/delete-a-file
cases.doc: A file deleted (bound to its path by the path's SHA-256) is gone; deleting it again is not_found (error 2); a folder is storage (error 21).

cases.name: file.delete/refused
cases.doc: The dev-menu marker (any case), /yaffs2 itself, paths outside /yaffs2, (1.13) /yaffs2/upgrade itself and anything in it, with a .. part or a control byte are refused for delete, rmdir and mkdir, before the confirmation is checked.

cases.name: file.delete/marker-with-its-token
cases.why_not: sends a delete of the dev-menu marker with a valid confirmation; the device guard allows paths outside the test area only with a token no path matches
cases.doc: The dev-menu marker cannot be deleted or removed even with the right confirmation: refused.

cases.name: file.delete/sha-and-bad-request
cases.doc: A confirmation that is not the path's SHA-256 is sha (nothing done); a request whose length does not match its path is bad_request.

cases.name: file.rmdir/empty-only
cases.doc: A folder that holds a file is state (error 93); a file is storage (error 20); once empty the folder is removed; again: not_found.

cases.name: file.mkdir/create
cases.doc: A new folder is ok and lists empty; the same name again is storage (error 17); a missing parent is not_found (error 2).

cases.name: file.mkdir/utf8-name
cases.doc: A folder named with non-ASCII UTF-8 is made, listed and removed by the same bytes.

cases.name: file.rename/a-file
cases.doc: 1.8: a file renamed (bound to both paths by their SHA-256) is found by its new name only; renaming the old name again is not_found (error 2), and so is a target whose folder does not exist.

cases.name: file.rename/a-folder
cases.doc: 1.8: a folder that holds a file is renamed as a whole (the file is found under the new name); a folder moved into itself is storage (error 22).

cases.name: file.rename/target-exists
cases.doc: 1.8: a target that exists, a file or a folder, is state (error 17): nothing is replaced.

cases.name: file.rename/utf8-name
cases.doc: 1.8: a file renamed to a non-ASCII UTF-8 name is read by the same bytes.

cases.name: file.rename/across-roots
cases.why_not: moves a file into the OS's content folder, outside the test area (the device pass moves only its own scratch files)
cases.doc: 1.8: a file moves from /yaffs2/xy-forever/ to /yaffs2/content/ and back.

cases.name: file.rename/refused
cases.doc: 1.8: a source or a target file.delete would refuse (the marker in any case, /yaffs2/upgrade or anything in it (1.13), a folder path ending in /, outside /yaffs2, a .. part) is refused before the confirmation is checked.

cases.name: file.rename/sha-and-bad-request
cases.doc: 1.8: a confirmation that is not the SHA-256 of both paths is sha (nothing done); a request without the target's NUL, or one byte short, is bad_request.

cases.name: file.write_begin/a-file
cases.doc: 1.18: a streamed write creates the file, and a second one replaces it in one step; data or an end without a write in progress is state; data at the wrong offset is range; a wrong SHA-256 is sha and leaves the target as it was.

steps.doc: a retry after a lost reply

cases.name: file.copy/a-file
cases.doc: 1.9: a file copied on the device (bound to both paths by their SHA-256) reads the same under both names; a copy onto a name that exists is state (error 17, nothing replaced); a missing source or target folder is not_found; a target below a file is storage with no partial target left; a source outside the write area that file.read reads is copied too.

cases.name: file.copy/refused
cases.doc: 1.9: a source file.read refuses (/yaffs2 itself, outside /yaffs2, a .. part) or a target file.write_staged refuses (the marker, /yaffs2/upgrade and anything in it (1.13), a folder path ending in /) is refused before the confirmation is checked.

cases.name: file.copy/sha-and-bad-request
cases.doc: 1.9: a confirmation that is not the SHA-256 of both paths is sha (nothing done); a request without the target's NUL, or one byte short, is bad_request.

cases.name: mods.apply/refused
cases.doc: 1.10: a mods.apply the device refuses before reading or writing anything: a profile or generation that is not one token, a machine list with an empty or bad id, too many extensions, a name with a space at its end, unknown flags, a request a byte short (bad_request); a confirmation that is not the SHA-256 of the request (sha).

cases.name: mods.apply/missing-input
cases.doc: 1.10: a well-formed, confirmed mods.apply whose base library entry does not exist is not_found with missing 1 (the base os.ldr); nothing is written.

cases.name: job.status/unknown-job
cases.doc: 1.10: job.status and job.cancel of a job id no job has (4294967295) are not_found; a request that is not one u32 is bad_request.

cases.name: boot.install/refusals
cases.why_not: boot.install writes the boot partition; it is never sent to a device by these runners
cases.doc: boot.install: state without a complete staging or with a wrong length, sha for a wrong token, image for a staged image that is no XY Forever build. A refusal before the writer runs leaves the staging as it was.

cases.name: boot.uninstall/refusals
cases.why_not: boot.uninstall writes the boot partition; it is never sent to a device by these runners
cases.doc: boot.uninstall: state without a complete staging, sha for a wrong token, image for anything but the stock 1.2.1 os.ldr.

cases.name: boot.uninstall/stock
cases.why_not: writes the boot partition (the OP-XY would boot stock 1.2.1 and lose this service)
cases.doc: The stock 1.2.1 os.ldr staged and confirmed: ok, the partition read back; log events while it runs; the staging is used up.

cases.name: boot.install/build
cases.why_not: writes the boot partition
cases.doc: A verified XY Forever build staged and confirmed: ok, the partition read back; log events; the staging is used up.

cases.name: device.reboot/to-the-menu
cases.doc: The reply comes first, then the connection drops; the port comes back, and the device needs hello again.

cases.name: device.reboot/no-target
cases.doc: Without a target the device restarts into the menu.

cases.name: device.reboot/odd-payload
cases.doc: A payload that is neither empty nor 4 bytes counts as no target: the device restarts into the menu.

cases.name: device.reboot/bad-target
cases.doc: A target above 2 is bad_request; the device stays.

cases.name: device.reboot/to-the-os
cases.why_not: boots the OS, which only a power cycle leaves
cases.doc: Target 1 restarts into the default firmware: the reply, then the connection drops. The simulator's power control brings the menu back.

cases.name: menu.continue/link
cases.doc: A mode above 1 or a payload that is neither empty nor 4 bytes is answered link (not bad_request); the menu stays.

cases.name: menu.continue/dry-run
cases.why_not: runs the boot path; the device pass's boot stage runs it on the device with its own checks
cases.doc: Mode 1: the whole boot path without starting the OS, then back to the menu (the connection drops and returns).

cases.name: menu.continue/boot
cases.why_not: boots the OS, which only a power cycle leaves
cases.doc: No mode: the menu closes and USB goes away after the ok reply.

cases.name: service.hold/bad-request
cases.doc: A value above 1 or a request that is not 4 bytes is bad_request and changes nothing.

cases.name: service.hold/on-off
cases.why_not: hold changes what every restart does until power-off; the device pass sets it itself and turns it off at the end
cases.doc: on 1 and on 0: ok.

cases.name: library.set_default/round-trip
cases.why_not: processor A writes a state slot (the default firmware)
cases.doc: Another entry, then back to the seeded default: ok, with the CRC-32 of the id sent to processor A.

cases.name: library.set_default/refusals
cases.why_not: library.set_default is never sent to a device by these runners (a valid id makes processor A write)
cases.doc: An id outside a-z 0-9 _ - or without its NUL is bad_request (id_hash 0); an id no entry has is storage, and the default stays.

cases.name: library.boot/refusals
cases.why_not: library.boot is never sent to a device by these runners (a right token for a usable entry boots it)
cases.doc: 1.7: a malformed id or a request without the token is bad_request, a wrong token sha, an id no entry has not_found: the status alone, nothing boots and the menu still answers.

cases.name: library.boot/boot
cases.why_not: boots the OS, which only a power cycle leaves
cases.doc: 1.7: a usable entry with its token: ok, then the menu closes and USB goes away (the entry boots once).

cases.name: tfw.check/not-a-package
cases.why_not: tfw.check first runs on a device in the OTP probe (scripts/tfw_probe.py, #15)
cases.doc: A file that is not a package: the check runs (ok) and fails with reason 2; no key is read, so the public-key hash is zero.

cases.name: tfw.check/errors
cases.why_not: tfw.check first runs on a device in the OTP probe (scripts/tfw_probe.py, #15)
cases.doc: A path without its NUL or outside /yaffs2/ is bad_request, a path the file policy refuses is refused, a missing file not_found: the status alone.

cases.name: tfw.check/unsigned
cases.why_not: it reads the device's keys from OTP: the first such read on a device is the OTP probe (#15)
cases.doc: A well-formed package header whose signature is not the vendor's fails with reason 6 (the simulator without the private keys: reason 4, no key); a public-key hash comes with reason 6.

cases.name: frame/noise-before-a-frame
cases.doc: The spec's stream, sent read by read: one reply per frame it lists, nothing else.

cases.name: frame/bad-crc
cases.doc: The spec's stream: the damaged frame is not answered.

steps.stream: a bad CRC, then a good frame

cases.name: frame/split-at-every-byte
cases.doc: The spec's stream: one byte per read.

steps.stream: a frame split at every byte

cases.name: frame/back-to-back
cases.doc: The spec's stream: two requests in one read are answered one by one, in order.

cases.name: frame/oversized-length
cases.doc: The spec's stream: a header announcing more than max_payload is noise.

cases.name: frame/cut-short
cases.doc: The spec's stream: a frame cut short swallows the start of the next one.

steps.stream: a frame cut short, then a frame

cases.name: frame/split-across-reads
cases.doc: The spec's stream: two frames cut into reads that span both.

cases.name: frame/cut-frame-idle-reset
cases.doc: A cut header announcing max_payload is dropped after idle_reset_ms of silence: the next hello is answered at once, nothing swallowed.
